entries.title: Optimal winning ply in the transversal achievement game (Guan's sharpness conjecture)

source.paper: The transversal achievement game on a square grid

entries.summary: For every n >= 4, the second player in the n x n transversal achievement game prevents a first-player win through ply 2n+1 via an (n-2)-matching invariant and an O-transversal counterthreat, proving with Guan's upper bound that the exact optimal winning ply is 2n+3.

entries.title: Connected chordal chord diagrams (Nabergall's Conjecture 8.5)

source.paper: The combinatorics of a tree-like functional equation for connected chord diagrams

entries.summary: For every n >= 1, the number of rooted chord diagrams of size n whose crossing graph is connected and chordal equals C_{n-1}^2 = ((1/n) binom(2n-2, n-1))^2, proved end-to-end in Lean 4 across 14 warning-free modules (NabergallChordalDiagrams.connectedChordalDiagram_card) via clique-boundary sector triangulation, earliest-cut irreducible factorization, and Clebsch–Gordan generating-function extraction.

entries.title: Petr–Turek temperate intersecting families (upper-half proof and exact n <= 8)

source.paper: Towards odd-sunflowers: temperate families and lightnings
source.journal: Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A 220 (2026)

entries.summary: Proves the sharp lightning upper bound L_k = (1/2) binom(2k, k) + binom(2k, k+1) + binom(2k-1, k+2) for every k >= 2 across the entire upper half of the Boolean cube (whenever at most one member has size < k), establishes an O(N_k / k^2) additive bound on the four central ranks (k >= 6), and proves by exact integer search that the unrestricted maxima on [4], [6], [8] are 7, 26, 98. Unrestricted k >= 5 remains open.

entries.title: Cardoso's subset synchronization conjecture (all weakly oriented circular automata)

source.paper: Synchronizing Automata: Open Problems (citing Cardoso, University of Porto PhD Thesis, 2014)

entries.summary: Proves Cardoso's exact ceiling bound B(n,m) = (n-1)^2 - (ceil(n/m)-1)(2n - m*ceil(n/m) - 1) sharply for every synchronizing weakly oriented circular automaton and every nonempty m-subset, removing both the unit-jump and rank-(n-1) restrictions of Cardoso's Theorem 5.7.8 via aggregate interval-growth counting across stage lengths. The general DFA conjecture remains open.

entries.title: Yuan–Parrilo permanent–sphere conjecture (order n <= 4, rank <= 3, and c > 5/6 bound)

source.authors: Chenyang Yuan and Pablo A. Parrilo
source.paper: Maximizing Products of Linear Forms, and The Permanent of Positive Semidefinite Matrices

entries.summary: Proves per(A) <= r(A) for every complex Hermitian positive semidefinite (HPSD) matrix of order n <= 4 and whenever (d)_{n-1} <= n^{n-1} (in particular n >= 2*rank(A) - 2, ruling out all rank <= 3 counterexamples; first open case (n=5, d=4)), and establishes the dimension-free exponential lower bound r(A) >= c^n per(A) with c = e exp(-sum_{j>=0} 2^{-j-1} log(1+2^j)) approx 0.836208 > 5/6 (improving e^{-gamma} approx 0.5615).

entries.title: Kashima–Ozeki odd coloring conjecture (all 4-trees and 5-trees)
entries.summary: Proves that every finite 4-tree is odd 6-colorable and every finite 5-tree is odd 7-colorable (both sharp, with no bound on vertex order) via exact integer bitset rooted-forest closure certificates (72 terminal forests for k=4; 917 terminal forests for k=5), settling the Kashima–Ozeki conjecture through k=5. The conjecture remains open for k >= 6.

entries.title: Eggert's 1971 conjecture in characteristic two (Kourovka Notebook 17.52)

source.authors: N. Eggert (annotated by L. S. Kazarin; eds. E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov)
source.paper: The Kourovka Notebook: Unsolved Problems in Group Theory (21st Edition); N. H. Eggert, Pacific J. Math. 36 (1971)

entries.summary: Every finite-dimensional commutative associative nilpotent algebra R over a finite (or any perfect) field k of characteristic two satisfies 2 dim_k R^(2) <= dim_k R with no restrictions on generators, grading, nilpotency class, or dim_k R^(2), proved end-to-end in Lean 4 (EggertNilpotentAlgebra.kourovka_17_52_char_two), resolving the characteristic-two case of Eggert's 1971 conjecture (Kourovka 17.52) and yielding the abelian-factor finite 2-group case of Kourovka 11.44 via Amberg–Kazarin's reduction. Odd primes p remain open.

entries.title: Counterexamples to the Sylvester characterization of linearly presented graded Möbius algebras (Fouli et al., Conjecture 4.1)

source.authors: Louiza Fouli, Sean Grate, Selvi Kara, Adam LaClair, Jason McCullough, Vinh Nguyen, Aleksandra Sobieska, and Prajwal Udanshive
source.paper: Graded Betti numbers of graded Möbius algebras of uniform matroids

entries.summary: Disproves the Sylvester-to-linear-presentation direction of Conjecture 4.1 of Fouli et al. (arXiv:2609.03827v1) via an infinite rank-3 family of quadratic Sylvester matroids indexed by F_2^m (m >= 3, starting at 15 points with beta_{2,4} = 20 and lower bound beta_{2,4} >= 2^{m-2}(2^m-1)(2^m-2)/6) and a 15-point quadratic Steiner triple system with every pair in a unique 3-circuit (beta_{2,4} = 4), each certified over Q by an explicit Koszul 2-cycle and separating boundary-killing functional. Proposition 4.4 of the paper proves the forward direction.

entries.title: Sharpness of the 2|G|^2 square-root overgroup bound (Kourovka Notebook 18.46)

source.authors: Ant. A. Klyachko (citing D. V. Baranov and Ant. A. Klyachko; eds. E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov)
source.paper: The Kourovka Notebook: Unsolved Problems in Group Theory (21st Edition); D. V. Baranov and Ant. A. Klyachko, Siber. Math. J. 53, no. 2 (2012), 201-206

entries.summary: Affirmatively resolves Kourovka Notebook 18.46: for every alternating group A_n with n >= 4096, any finite overgroup in which (1 2 3 4)(5 6) has a square root has order at least 2|A_n|^2 (matching the wreath-product upper bound 2|G|^2, proved via CFSG), and independently without CFSG the dihedral group D_8 requires minimum simultaneous square-root host order 128 = 2|D_8|^2 (exhausting all 16 marked index-two kernels of order 16 in verify.py).

entries.title: Carving-width and elementary-abelian Petersen-lift obstructions to 5-edge-connected 5-regular class 2 multigraphs

source.authors: Yulai Ma, Davide Mattiolo, Eckhard Steffen, and Isaak H. Wolf
source.paper: Pairwise disjoint perfect matchings in r-edge-connected r-regular graphs

entries.summary: Proves that every 5-edge-connected 5-regular loopless multigraph of carving width at most 7 (via 7 parity-allowed port templates across 20,979 oriented joins), as well as every 5-edge-connected F_p^d-voltage lift (p in {2,3,5,7}, d >= 0) of P+M+N for perfect matchings M, N of the Petersen graph P (via exact cubic profiles and 131 verified 50-vertex quintic colorings), is 5-edge-colorable, while edge-connectivity 4 is sharp across cyclic covers of every degree n >= 2 without triple edges. Ma–Mattiolo–Steffen–Wolf Problem 1.6 remains open in general.

entries.title: Conway's thrackle conjecture: 5(n-1)/4 upper bound, settlement for n <= 15, and musquash exclusions

source.authors: John H. Conway (recorded by D. R. Woodall, 1971); Dániel Gábor Simon (2026 upper bound)
source.paper: Conway's thrackle conjecture: a new upper bound of 4n/3 (Dániel Gábor Simon, Oct 2026); D. R. Woodall, Thrackles and deadlock (1971)
source.target: Conway's Thrackle Conjecture (m <= n) and Global Edge-Bound Problem

entries.summary: Settles Conway's thrackle conjecture (m <= n) for all graphs on n <= 15 vertices (improving n <= 12) plus four 16-vertex minimal bicyclic obstructions via audited strict-RUP SAT/LRAT refutations, lowers the global upper bound from floor(4(n-1)/3) to floor(5(n-1)/4) for all n >= 5 via zero-curvature discharging (combinatorial discharging and forest reduction formalized in Lean 4), proves 5/4 is the exact sharpness wall of the NSB(16) embedding framework via girth-8 periodic witnesses and a 255-vertex dual showing Theta(1,7,9) necessity, and excludes all distinct cycles of length <= 7 sharing a vertex with any standard odd or Woodall distinct musquash. Conway's full conjecture remains open for general n >= 16.

entries.title: Thompson's cyclic matrix permutation conjecture (Kourovka 16.95): rank-one finite fields and unrestricted GL(5,2)–GL(7,2)

source.authors: J. G. Thompson (eds. E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov)
source.paper: The Kourovka Notebook: Unsolved Problems in Group Theory (21st Edition)

entries.summary: Proves Thompson's cyclic column-ordering conjecture for every invertible rank-one perturbation of a scalar permutation matrix over F_2, F_3, and F_4 in every dimension (with no support restrictions), and over every fixed finite field F_q in all dimensions n >= N(q) via an explicit zero-sum block partition and two-cycle criterion. Independently verifies all unrestricted matrices in GL(5,2) (exact minimum 24 = 4! cyclic orders), GL(6,2) (139,629 orbit-cover representatives), and GL(7,2) (28,892,664 orbit-cover representatives, available via --seven). General rank in arbitrary dimension remains open.

entries.title: Herzog–Schönheim conjecture for all finite almost simple groups (Kourovka 21.93 / Erdős #274)

source.authors: M. Herzog and J. Schönheim (annotated by L. Margolis; eds. E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov)
source.paper: The Kourovka Notebook: Unsolved Problems in Group Theory (21st Edition); Erdős Problem #274

entries.summary: Proves the Herzog–Schönheim conjecture (Kourovka 21.93 / Erdős #274) for every finite almost simple group S <= G <= Aut(S), overcoming Garonzi–Margolis Remark 5.1 (unbounded reciprocal index sums) via a filled-fibre capacity criterion K(m) D(N) < 1 (counting step formalized in Lean 4) combined with CFSG and exact rational verification across all classical, exceptional, alternating, sporadic, and Tits families (complementing Menon's Nov 2026 solvable proof). General non-almost-simple nonsolvable groups remain open.

entries.title: 2-degenerate linear arboricity conjecture (Basavaraju et al., Conjecture 2): odd-cycle packing, paired neighborhoods, mad(G) <= 3, and 9-vertex sharpness

source.authors: Manu Basavaraju, Arijit Bishnu, Mathew Francis, and Drimit Pattanayak
source.paper: The linear arboricity conjecture for graphs of low degeneracy

entries.summary: Partially resolves Basavaraju–Bishnu–Francis–Pattanayak Conjecture 2 (2-linear colorability of 2-degenerate graphs with Delta <= 4): proves 2-linear colorability (at most 1 defect) when G has no two edge-disjoint odd cycles, proves prescribed-pair defect flexibility whenever every degree-4 neighborhood has a perfect matching (covering all claw-free 2-degenerate graphs and iterated twin-cap, pendant-triangle, long-ear, and double-subdivision closures), settles the density equality endpoint mad(G) <= 3 for all subquartic graphs (extending J.-L. Wu's 1999 strict mad(G) < 3 bound), and proves sharpness of the |E| >= 2|V|-5 one-defect threshold via a 9-vertex, 12-edge graph forcing exactly 2 defects (formalized in Lean 4) plus infinite families forcing (2|V|-|E|)/3 defects. The unrestricted 2-degenerate Delta <= 4 conjecture remains open.

entries.title: Disproof of Gaetz–Gao's strong hull property conjecture for Coxeter groups (Conjecture 1.2)

source.paper: The hull metric on Coxeter groups

entries.summary: Unconditionally disproves Gaetz–Gao Conjecture 1.2 (both the strong hull property and the weaker ordinary hull property, showing log |Conv(-,-)| is not a metric on Coxeter groups in general) in the affine Coxeter group W(A3~), formalized end-to-end in Lean 4 on Mathlib's presented Coxeter group via an exact l1-isometry into Z^6 and two-point Phi-box theorem (422 theorems, zero sorry, standard axioms only). Exact zero-float computation also verifies minimal counterexamples (60*121 = 7260 < 7921 ordinary; 96*97 = 9312 < 9825 strong), and the written proof extends the disproof to every irreducible affine Coxeter group of rank >= 4 (completing the affine dichotomy with Liu's 2025 rank-3 proof).

entries.title: Gessel–Zhuang Conjecture 7.1 (inverse peak real-rootedness): all 7 families at every fixed count and unconditional first mixed rows

source.authors: Ira M. Gessel and Yan Zhuang
source.paper: Two-sided permutation statistics via symmetric functions

entries.summary: Proves eventual real-rootedness (all zeros real, nonpositive, and simple for non-elementary rows) for every part (a)-(g) of Gessel-Zhuang Conjecture 7.1 at every fixed conditioning count k for all sufficiently large n >= N(k) via triangular generating-function extraction and Popov-Sedletskii Mittag-Leffler root localization. Independently proves unconditional real-rootedness at every n >= 1 for all elementary rows (r <= 2) and for the first non-elementary mixed rows ((a)-(d) at k = 1 and (e)-(g) at k = 3) by explicit n >= 40 trigonometric error bounds plus exact zero-float integer Sturm-chain certification through n = 39. Uniform-in-k real-rootedness for all pairs (n, k) remains open.

entries.title: Tuza's 1981 conjecture: universal bound 14*tau(G) <= 39*nu(G) and colored-family bound 21/8

source.paper: A Bound Below 2.8 for Tuza's Conjecture (Sichen Wang, Sept 2026); Z. Tuza, Graphs and Combinatorics 6 (1990), 373-380
source.target: Tuza's Conjecture (tau(G) <= 2*nu(G)) and Universal Constant Bound

entries.summary: Proves the universal bound 14*tau(G) <= 39*nu(G) (tau(G) <= (39/14)*nu(G) approx 2.7857*nu(G)) for every finite simple graph G via simultaneous triangle-book rotation on distinct red opposites, safe opposite switching, and a 6-inequality rational cover certificate—improving both Sichen Wang's Sept 2026 record (165/59 approx 2.7966, arXiv:2609.13831v1) and Tyler B. Hughes's Nov 2026 unrefereed draft (81/29 approx 2.7931). Also proves the sharper red-blue colored-family bound 8*tau_R(G) + 5*|private| <= 21*nu_R(G) (21/8 = 2.625 < 8/3). Formalized end-to-end in Lean 4 on Mathlib's SimpleGraph (552 theorems, zero sorry, standard axioms only, MIT-licensed adaptation of Wang's tuza-lean base). Partially resolves Tuza's conjecture by lowering the universal constant; tau(G) <= 2*nu(G) remains open.
